funder: Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) & Bankers' Committee
who_can_apply: Existing creative enterprises and start-ups in fashion, IT, movie and music (plus students in software development); apply through participating banks (PFIs)
typical_award: Loans of NGN 3m to NGN 50m depending on vertical (NGN 500m for movie distribution)
usual_window: Ongoing / no fixed window stated (scheme est. 2018)
notes: LOAN, not a grant. Verified on CBN page. Bank pages (e.g. GTBank, Polaris) describe 9% p.a.; not stated on CBN page. Activity level of the scheme in 2026 not confirmed.

programme: Nigerian Creative and Entertainment Industry Loan Scheme (NCEILS)
who_can_apply: Companies registered in Nigeria operating in entertainment/creative incl. music production & distribution; not government-owned
typical_award: Not stated (tenor up to 7 years incl. moratorium)
usual_window: Ongoing / no window stated
notes: LOAN. Requires incorporation docs, 3 yrs audited accounts, business plan, IP valuation for collateral. Suits labels/management companies more than individual artists.

funder: Bank of Industry (BOI) / iDICE (FG, AfDB, AFD, IsDB)
who_can_apply: Registered technology and creative businesses operating in Nigeria, explicitly incl. music, performing arts, digital content
typical_award: NGN 10m to NGN 1bn; max 10% p.a.; up to 6-month moratorium; up to 5-yr repayment
usual_window: Listed as 'Applications Open' on 2026-10-11 (apply via idice.boi.ng)
notes: LOAN (US$45m facility). Open at check date.

who_can_apply: Eligible Nigerian tech and creative start-ups seeking productive asset finance (equipment, creative infrastructure); open regardless of faith
typical_award: Not stated per applicant (US$65m facility)
usual_window: Listed as 'Applications Open' on 2026-10-11 (idice.boi.ng or Lotus, SunTrust, Summit banks)
notes: Sharia-compliant cost-plus asset finance, not a grant.

who_can_apply: Idea/validation-stage founders aged 18–35 operating from any Nigerian state or FCT; 12-week programme (digital/creative)
typical_award: Non-equity funding of up to NGN 10,000,000 for those who complete programme milestones
usual_window: Cohort 2 applications closed (per idice.ng, Oct 2026); next window not announced
notes: Grant is conditional on completing training. Growth Lab (post-MVP, equity-based) 'to be announced'.

funder: Federal Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism & the Creative Economy (FMACTCE)
who_can_apply: Nigerian creative businesses (music & entertainment included); Phase 1 for projects > US$100k, Phase 2 for MSMEs < US$100k
typical_award: Up to US$100,000 prioritised in Phase 2 (debt, quasi-equity, equity; IP as collateral)
usual_window: 2025: Phase 1 28 Apr–30 May 2025; Phase 2 4 Aug–1 Sep 2025
notes: Windows from FMACTCE rollout doc (fmacce.gov.ng PDF) and fmino.gov.ng. PARTIALLY VERIFIED: cedf.gov.ng only shows overview. Press (afrobeatswire, 5 Oct 2026) reports disbursement still not done as of Sep 2026. Treat as uncertain.

programme: Project SURGE – creative economy loans (successor to MSME Loan Programme)
who_can_apply: MSMEs and young entrepreneurs resident and operating in Lagos State, incl. creative economy businesses
typical_award: NGN 100,000 to NGN 5m at 9% p.a. with 5% equity contribution (SURGE, per press)
usual_window: Launched Jul 2026; applications via LSETF loan portal (no closing date found)
notes: LOAN. PARTIALLY VERIFIED: SURGE terms from BusinessDay (1 Aug 2026) and LSETF LinkedIn; no SURGE page found on lsetf.ng. URL is LSETF's MSME loan page (9% p.a., up to NGN 5m SME loans).

funder: Mastercard Foundation / Terra Academy for the Arts (TAFTA) with FCMB
programme: Art & Entrepreneurship Academy – FCMB Creative Industry Fund
who_can_apply: Young Nigerian creatives (programme targets 65,600 youth, 70% female) – training plus access to a creative loan fund
typical_award: Not stated (no-collateral, single-digit-interest loans)
usual_window: Programme active 2022–2027; no window stated
notes: This is the only Mastercard Foundation creative programme found that covers Nigeria; its Kenya programmes (Sanara, KICP) do not. Loan, not grant. Contact TAFTA/FCMB for terms.

funder: UK FCDO / UK-Nigeria Tech Hub (implemented by Tech4Dev)
who_can_apply: Registered Nigerian creative companies incl. music labels/studios with a specific technical production gap; must attach 2–5 mid-career creatives and do a give-back activity
typical_award: Flexible grant size by scope (3 tiers); no figure stated
usual_window: 2026: 22 Apr–30 Jul 2026 (closed)
notes: First-phase pilot; recurrence not announced.

who_can_apply: Artists, cultural professionals, organisations, collectives; must partner with at least one UK-based partner
country_eligibility: Nigeria listed (plus ~35 other countries and UK)
typical_award: GBP 5,000–15,000 overall; max GBP 10,000 for UK–Nigeria projects
usual_window: 2026: 17 Jun–12 Aug 2026 (closed); outcomes from 14 Oct 2026
notes: Replaces International Collaboration Grants. Music eligible. British Council also running UK/Nigeria Season 2028 EOI (closed 14 Sep 2026, not a funding call).

funder: U.S. Consulate General Lagos (Public Diplomacy Section)
programme: U.S.–Nigeria Creative, Digital & Innovation Economy Initiative (APS PDS-APS-FY26-01)
who_can_apply: US or Nigerian non-profits and higher-education institutions only (for-profits not eligible); themes include music co-production, streaming/digital rights
typical_award: USD 20,000–60,000 (4–10 awards; cost share required)
usual_window: FY26: posted 22 Jul 2026, deadline 20 Aug 2026 (archived 19 Sep 2026)
notes: Annual Program Statement; artists would apply via an NGO. Deadline date from govtribe summary of the NOFO; award range and dates on simpler.grants.gov.

programme: Public Diplomacy Annual Notice of Funding Opportunity (PDS-ABV-NOFO)
who_can_apply: Nigerian non-profits and educational institutions in the 19 northern states and FCT; programmes need a US cultural/expert element
usual_window: FY25: posted 13 Jan 2025, closed Mar 2025 (archived 20 Apr 2025); FY26 round not seen
notes: Not music-specific; arts/cultural projects possible. Listing at ng.usembassy.gov/grants.

funder: Chocolate City Group – Founders Fund Africa (with Argentil Capital, CcHUB)
programme: Founders Fund Africa Creative Economy Accelerator
who_can_apply: Start-ups in music, film, gaming, content creation or creative tech; at least one founder of Nigerian descent; business located in Africa
typical_award: USD 20,000–50,000 per start-up via convertible notes (10 start-ups)
usual_window: 2026 (inaugural): opened Jul 2026, closed 28 Aug 2026
notes: INVESTMENT (convertible note), not a grant. Amount on official site; deadline from press (BusinessDay, TechCabal). Site still carries template placeholder text.

who_can_apply: Founders aged 18+ from any of the 54 African countries with a business idea or business up to ~5 years old, any sector (creative businesses incl.)
typical_award: USD 5,000 non-refundable seed capital + training & mentorship
usual_window: Annually 1 Jan–1 Mar (2026 cycle closed; cohort announced 22 Mar 2026)
notes: Not music-specific but widely used by artist-entrepreneurs/managers. Seed paid only after training, business plan and due diligence.

who_can_apply: African recording artists and record labels with a history of strong sales (production and distribution of music)
typical_award: Not stated per deal (part of a US$2bn creative-industries facility)
usual_window: Ongoing / no window stated
notes: DEBT financing for established acts/labels. Source is Afreximbank's own CANEX brochure on a CANEX staging domain; portal page (portal.afreximbank.com/our-solutions/music-development-finance) did not load. Apply via portal.afreximbank.com.

who_can_apply: Amateur, emerging and established creators across Africa, individuals or teams; build a working project in a 4-day sprint
typical_award: Per category: 1st USD 7,000; 2nd USD 3,500; 3rd USD 1,500; finalists USD 500 (pool USD 50,000)
usual_window: 2026: registration 30 Jul–19 Aug 2026; sprint 20–24 Aug 2026 (closed)
notes: Competition prize, not grant. 2026 appears to be first edition. Winners attend CANEX WKND, Lagos, 5–8 Nov 2026.

who_can_apply: Africans on the continent or in the diaspora, under 35, incl. musicians; 2+ yrs experience, 5,000+ followers; must first join ANF's African Narrative Collective
usual_window: Rolling, open until end of year or until 12–14 storytellers selected
notes: Work must challenge stereotypes about Africa. No equipment or event-attendance costs.

funder: Africa No Filter with Comic Relief
who_can_apply: Individual storytellers 18+ (content creators, podcasters, journalists, muralists etc.) with 5,000+ followers, unsigned; climate/debt/gender theme
country_eligibility: Nigeria + Mozambique, Uganda, Angola, Chad, Rep. Congo, Tanzania, South Sudan, Malawi, Zambia
typical_award: Up to USD 4,000
usual_window: 2026: 11 Aug–25 Sep 2026 (closed)
notes: Thematic and not music-specific; artists who make content could qualify.

programme: SOFACO – Solidarity Fund for Artists and Cultural Organisations
who_can_apply: Professional artists residing and working in Africa with 5+ yrs experience, or cultural organisations registered in Africa with 3+ yrs activity
usual_window: 6th call: 15 Apr–15 May 2025; no 2026 grant call seen
notes: Six SOFACO calls since 2020. ACF's current call (15 Sep–16 Oct 2026) is LEWO Africa, an online leadership boot camp for women, not a grant.

who_can_apply: Emerging artists (any genre) registered for ACCES 2026 who can attend in Johannesburg on 29–30 Oct 2026; submit one original song
typical_award: One winner: Music In Africa promo package worth ZAR 35,000 (studio time, video, press, radio help)
usual_window: 2026: deadline 16 Oct 2026 (OPEN at check date)
notes: In-kind prize. Travel to Johannesburg at applicant's cost. MIAF's Sound Connects Fund ended in 2024 (Southern Africa only) so it is left out.

programme: AOCA – Support for cultural operators in Africa
who_can_apply: African cultural organisations based in Africa (or French cultural network); needs a support letter from the French network (e.g. Alliance Française / IF in Nigeria); tours, festivals, co-creation
typical_award: EUR 5,000–15,000, up to 50% of project budget
usual_window: 2026 call: 1 Jul–30 Oct 2026 (OPEN) for projects Mar–Dec 2027
notes: Best Alliance Française/Institut français route for Nigerian music organisations. Tours need 5+ shows in 3+ African countries.

funder: Africa-Europe Partnerships for Culture – Connect & Create (EU; Goethe-Institut, Expertise France, Institut français)
programme: Connect & Create #Circulation: Live Performance and Music Circulation 2027
who_can_apply: Organisations based in sub-Saharan Africa or the EU: ensembles, labels, production offices, festivals, venues, artist development agencies
typical_award: Up to 70% of project budget (mobility costs); min 30% co-financing
usual_window: 2027 call: 9 Jul–30 Sep 2026 (closed); projects Feb–Dec 2027
notes: Programme runs 2025–2028. Official call on ifprog.emundus.fr (cid=353) not fetched; details from MIAF repost and Création Africa. Africa tours need 5 shows in 3 countries.

programme: Individual Mobility Grants for Artists and Cultural Professionals
who_can_apply: Individual artists/culture professionals 18+ based in sub-Saharan Africa or the EU, all disciplines incl. music; mainly Africa–Africa travel
typical_award: Up to EUR 4,000 (travel, accommodation, per diem, project costs)
usual_window: Rolling with quarterly cut-offs; next 15 Dec 2026; final cut-off 15 Sep 2027
notes: Fixed-term scheme (2025–2028). Amount and cut-offs from Goethe-Institut Rwanda page; eligibility from Goethe call PDF.

who_can_apply: Performing arts and music professionals/structures in the 48 sub-Saharan countries or the EU; 16 hubs selected, then Creative Tandem projects
typical_award: Not stated
usual_window: 2026: 15 Sep–13 Oct 2026 (OPEN at check date); programme starts early 2027
notes: Training, networking and project support rather than a straight grant. Fixed-term EU programme to 2028.

who_can_apply: Professional artists/ensembles/organisations based outside Germany co-producing new music, theatre, dance or performance work with partners in Germany; developing countries welcome
typical_award: EUR 15,000–30,000 (max 75% of costs)
usual_window: Two rounds a year: 15 Jan–1 Apr 2026 and 17 Aug–12 Oct 2026 (OPEN, closes 12 Oct 2026)
notes: Must contact the local Goethe-Institut (Lagos) before applying. Music recordings, tours and purely commercial projects are excluded.

who_can_apply: Individual early-career artists (1–5 yrs professional practice) from and living in eligible countries, whose work addresses social/political issues
typical_award: EUR 5,000 trust-based grant
usual_window: Annual; 2026 call closed 8 Jan 2026
notes: 100 awards a year. The Fund notes Nigeria is heavily oversubscribed and cannot be awarded in proportion to applications. No groups.

who_can_apply: Individual mid-career artists (~8–15 yrs) in thematic programmes, e.g. Building Beyond (Africa), CAREC (climate), Moving Narratives
typical_award: EUR 10,000 + year-long programme
usual_window: Varies by programme (e.g. Building Beyond Cycle 5 closed 13 Aug 2025)
notes: Themes rarely music-specific; fit depends on the cycle.

who_can_apply: Artists/cultural practitioners (individuals or duos) permanently resident in West, Central, East or Southern Africa, all disciplines incl. music
typical_award: Fully funded up to 3 months: accommodation, travel, per diem; production contribution on request
usual_window: Annually 1 Jan–1 Mar; residency the following year
notes: Students not eligible.

who_can_apply: Two artist partners: one with a Swiss connection, one active in a Pro Helvetia liaison region (Africa list incl. Nigeria); collaboration must come from a prior residency/research trip/joint project
typical_award: Not stated (artist fees, travel, co-creation costs)
usual_window: Annually 1 Jan–1 Jun; decision 1 Oct
notes: Only useful if there is already a Swiss partner.

who_can_apply: Public institutions and NGOs from developing countries that are Parties to the 2005 Convention (plus INGOs); structural projects, not production of works
typical_award: Up to USD 100,000 for 12–24 months
usual_window: Annual; 17th call 23 Mar–6 May 2026 (closed)
notes: For music NGOs/associations, not individual artists. Nigeria's place on the 2026 eligible-country annex was NOT checked (annex PDF blocked); Nigeria is believed to be a Party but confirm before applying.

who_can_apply: Developing independent artists (not signed directly to a major) with an upcoming release with music video; Rising is for earlier-stage artists, label-agnostic
country_eligibility: Global (no country restriction stated; Nigerian alumni incl. Tems, Rema)
typical_award: Grant/seed funding amount not stated; Rising gives micro-grants
usual_window: Twice-yearly classes; Fall 2026 window closed (H1 2026 closed 25 Mar 2026)
notes: Rising has no open application process.

who_can_apply: Threatened artists from any country/discipline facing severe targeted threats; placed at host institutions in safe countries
typical_award: Fellowship (up to 1 year) paid via host; amount not stated
usual_window: NOT currently accepting new applications (paused at check date)
notes: Emergency/safety route only. Kept because paused, not ended.

who_can_apply: Organisations working on arts and inequality; most grants identified by Ford staff
typical_award: Not stated
usual_window: No open call; Ford does not accept unsolicited proposals (only JustFilms documentary submissions, currently closed)
notes: INVITATION ONLY. Listed so the tool can say why it cannot be applied to. Ford is a major ANF funder, so ANF grants are the indirect route.

who_can_apply: Cross-border collaborative music projects with collaborators from 2+ countries/traditions (per third-party guide)
typical_award: Not stated (crowd-matched; seasonal pools of a few thousand USD per third-party leaderboard)
usual_window: Seasonal (Artizen 'seasons'); dates not verified
notes: UNVERIFIED: official page needs sign-in; details from paragraph.com guide and an unofficial artizen.fyi tracker. May not be the 'Global Music Fund' you meant; no other programme with that name was found.

funder: Arab Fund for Arts and Culture (AFAC)
who_can_apply: Individuals from the 22 Arab League states (any residence), and institutions with Arab-region projects; production, recording, performance, festivals, podcasts
country_eligibility: Arab League incl. Egypt, Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Sudan, Mauritania, Somalia, Djibouti, Comoros – NOT Nigeria
typical_award: Up to USD 25,000 individuals/teams; up to USD 35,000 collectives/institutions
usual_window: Annual second call: 15 Apr–19 Jun 2026; announcement Nov 2026
notes: North/Horn of Africa only.

funder: France Médias Monde / RFI (with Institut français, Sacem, OIF)
who_can_apply: Emerging professional artists/groups who are nationals and residents of OIF-member countries in Africa, Indian Ocean, Caribbean; at least 1 album or 2 EPs/8 tracks
country_eligibility: Francophone (OIF) Africa – NOT Nigeria (not an OIF member)
typical_award: EUR 10,000 + RFI concert + Institut français Africa tour
usual_window: Annual; 2026 edition 6 Oct–20 Nov 2025 (next likely Oct–Nov 2026)
notes: Ghana, Egypt etc. are in OIF list in the rules; Nigeria is not.

who_can_apply: SAMRO member composers/authors/publishers; 3-year cooling-off for past CSI recipients
typical_award: Up to ZAR 25,000 per recipient (ZAR 3m pool, 120 grants in 2026)
usual_window: 2026 cycle closed 7 Nov 2025; annual since 2021
notes: Collecting-society creation fund; included as a model. Nigerian collecting societies were not researched for this list.

who_can_apply: Young women and men in creative work (incl. live music) in 6 Kenyan counties: financing, skills, business support
typical_award: Not stated
usual_window: Active 2024–2027; rolling opportunities
notes: Fixed-term programme.

funder: PRS Foundation (with DBT, British Council, PPL, ACE etc.)
who_can_apply: UK-based artists, bands, songwriters, producers formally invited to international industry showcases or song camps
country_eligibility: UK-based only – NOT open to artists living in Nigeria
typical_award: Up to GBP 8,250
usual_window: Rolling, with set deadlines for high-demand events (e.g. SXSW)
notes: Useful only for UK-based Nigerian diaspora acts. No PRS Foundation scheme open to non-UK residents was found.

programme: MOBO Amplified (formerly MOBO Help Musicians Fund)
who_can_apply: Working musicians 18+ creating music of Black origin, living in the UK with right to work, UK bank account, 40% income from music
country_eligibility: UK residents only – NOT open to artists living in Nigeria
typical_award: Up to GBP 3,000 + 12-month programme (15 places)
usual_window: Annual summer window (2026 cohort opened 1 Jun 2026); currently closed
notes: For UK-based Afrobeats/diaspora artists only.
